questions.q: If the surrounding air is kept at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and a body cools from $80^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 30 minutes, then temperature of the body after one hour will be
questions.solution:
By Newton's law of cooling, we write

\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto\left(\theta-\theta_0\right) \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{k}\left(\theta-\theta_0\right) \Rightarrow \int\left(\frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\theta-\theta_0}\right)=\int \mathrm{kdt} \\
& \therefore \log \left|\theta-\theta_0\right|=\mathrm{kt}+\mathrm{c} \\
& \text { When } \mathrm{t}=0, \theta=80 \text { and } \theta_0=25 \\
& \therefore \log |80-25|=0+\mathrm{c} \quad \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\log |55| \\
& \text { When } \mathrm{t}=30, \theta=50 \\
& \therefore \log |50-25|=30 \mathrm{k}+\log |55| \\
& \therefore \mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{30} \log \left|\frac{5}{11}\right|
\end{aligned}

From (1), (2), (3) we write

\log \left|\theta-\theta_0\right|=\frac{1}{30} \log \left|\frac{5}{11}\right| t+\log |55|

questions.solution:
Perfect black body absorption and emission

A perfectly black body absorbs all incident radiation regardless of wavelength, giving it an absorption coefficient $a = 1$.

Kirchhoff's law establishes that emissivity equals absorptivity at a given wavelength and temperature: $e = a$.

Since $a = 1$, the emissivity must also be unity: $e = 1$.

A perfectly black body is therefore both a perfect absorber and perfect emitter of radiation.

The correct choice is $\boxed{B}$.
